S&T Bancorp Inc. (NASDAQ:STBA) reported Monday that its board of directors approved a limited waiver of the mandatory retirement age for Jeffrey D. Grube, the company’s Lead Independent Director. The information comes from a statement included in the company’s recent SEC filing.
According to the filing, effective January 28, 2026, the board granted Mr. Grube a waiver from the corporate bylaws and governance guidelines that require directors to retire at age 72. Mr. Grube, who reached the mandatory retirement age in January 2026, abstained from the board vote on this matter.
The waiver allows Mr. Grube to remain eligible for nomination to the board through the 2028 annual shareholders meeting and, if elected, to serve until the 2029 annual shareholders meeting. The board may choose to nominate him each year and may continue to appoint him as Lead Independent Director during this period. The board stated that it does not intend to permanently amend the retirement age provisions in its bylaws or governance guidelines.
Mr. Grube has served as Lead Independent Director since September 24, 2025. The SEC filing notes that he does not qualify as a “Grandfathered Director” under the company’s bylaws, which would have allowed service until age 75 for certain directors.
The company’s bylaws, as cited in the filing, generally require directors to retire at the first annual meeting following their 72nd birthday, unless they are classified as Grandfathered Directors. Upon retirement due to age, directors may be appointed as Director Emeritus for up to three years.
